source_text: Quos imitantur scilicet adque sectantur qui Dei traditione contempta alienas doctrinas adpetunt et magisteria humanae institutionis inducunt: quos increpat Dominus et obiurgat in euangelio suo dicens: reicitis mandatum Dei, ut traditionem uestram statuatis. peius hoc crimen est quam quod admisisse lapsi uidentur, qui tamen in paenitentia criminis constitute Deum plenis satisfactionibus deprecantur. hic ecclesia quaeritur et rogatur, illic ecclesiae repugnatur: hic potest necessitas fuisse, illic uoluntas tenetur in scelere: hic qui lapsus est sibi tantum nocuit, illic qui haeresin uel schisma facere conatus est multos secum trahendo decepit: hic animae unius est damnum, illic periculum plurimorum. certe peccasse se hic et intellegit et lamentatur et plangit, ille tumens in peccato suo et in ipsis sibi delictis placens a matre filios segregat, oues a pastore sollicitat, Dei sacramenta disturbat. et cum lapsus semel peccauerit, ille cottidie peccat. postremo lapsus martyrium postmodum consecutus potest regni promissa percipere: ille si extra ecclesiam fuerit occisus, ad ecclesiae non potest praemia peruenire.
thought_title: The greater guilt of schismatics compared with the lapsed
orientation: Cyprian is contrasting those who have lapsed under persecution but repent with those who deliberately break Church unity by introducing false teachings.
pass_a_gloss: Whom certainly they imitate and follow who, with God's tradition despised, seek after foreign doctrines and introduce teachings of human institution: whom the Lord rebukes and reproves in his gospel, saying: you reject the commandment of God, so that you may establish your own tradition. This crime is worse than that which the lapsed seem to have committed, who nevertheless, established in repentance of the crime, entreat God with full satisfactions. Here the Church is sought and asked for, there the Church is fought against: here there could have been necessity, there will is held in wickedness: here he who has lapsed has harmed only himself, there he who has attempted to make heresy or schism has deceived many by dragging them with him: here there is the loss of one soul, there the danger of many. Certainly this one both understands that he has sinned and laments and bewails, that one swelling in his sin and pleasing himself in his very offenses separates sons from the mother, entices sheep away from the shepherd, disturbs the sacred signs of God. And while the lapsed has sinned once, that one sins daily. Finally the lapsed, having afterward obtained martyrdom, can receive the promised things of the kingdom: that one, if he has been killed outside the Church, cannot attain to the rewards of the Church.

choices.why: Ablative absolute; keeps the passive force of contempta and the source-order emphasis on the tradition being set aside.
Magisteria is plural and concrete; 'teachings' preserves the plural and the contrast with God's tradition.

choices.term: reicitis mandatum Dei, ut traditionem uestram statuatis
choices.english: you reject the commandment of God, so that you may establish your own tradition
choices.why: The ut clause is purpose; 'so that you may establish' keeps the subjunctive force and the second-person plural address.
rejected: you reject God's commandment to establish your tradition
rejecting the commandment of God, you establish your tradition

choices.why: Satisfactiones is a technical term for acts of penance; the plural is kept to preserve the concrete sense.
Tenetur is passive; the will is caught or held fast in the crime, emphasizing deliberate persistence.

choices.english: disturbs the sacred signs of God
choices.why: Sacramenta is plural and refers to the sacred signs or mysteries of the Church; 'disturbs' keeps the violent force of disturbat.
rejected: overturns the sacred signs of God

pass_b_english: Those who despise God's tradition and seek after foreign doctrines, introducing teachings of human institution, are clearly imitating and following these men. The Lord rebukes and reproaches them in his Gospel, saying: "You reject the commandment of God, so that you may establish your own tradition" (Mark 7:9). This crime is worse than the one the lapsed seem to have committed—yet they, having been placed in repentance for their sin, entreat God with full satisfactions. In the one case the Church is sought and asked for; in the other the Church is fought against. In the one case there could have been necessity; in the other the will is held fast in wickedness. The one who lapsed harmed only himself, but the one who has tried to create heresy or schism has deceived many by dragging them along with him. In the one case there is the loss of a single soul; in the other there is danger for many. Certainly the one who lapsed both understands and laments and mourns that he has sinned, but the other, swelling in his sin and pleasing himself in his very offenses, separates children from their mother, entices sheep away from the shepherd, and disturbs the sacred signs of God. And while the lapsed person has sinned once, the other sins daily. Finally, the lapsed person who afterward obtains martyrdom can receive the promises of the kingdom; but if the heretic is killed outside the Church, he cannot arrive at the rewards of the Church.

problems.quote: but the one who is killed outside the Church cannot arrive at the rewards of the Church
problems.source_quote: ille si extra ecclesiam fuerit occisus, ad ecclesiae non potest praemia peruenire
problems.why: English omits 'si' (if) - 'if he is killed outside the Church.' The English 'who is killed' makes it a definite statement rather than conditional. This changes modality from conditional possibility to assertion.
problems.fix: but if he is killed outside the Church, he cannot arrive at the rewards of the Church
problems.ruling: 'si extra ecclesiam fuerit occisus' is conditional; 'who is killed' drops 'si', changing meaning from hypothetical to assertion.

edits.old: but the one who is killed outside the Church cannot arrive at the rewards of the Church.
edits.new: but if he is killed outside the Church, he cannot arrive at the rewards of the Church.

fixed: Added the conditional 'if' to match the source's 'si extra ecclesiam fuerit occisus' (if he has been killed outside the Church), preserving the conditional modality.

problems.quote: if he is killed outside the Church
problems.source_quote: ille si extra ecclesiam fuerit occisus
problems.why: The Latin 'ille' refers back to the heretic/schismatic, not the lapsed person. The English 'if he is killed' ambiguously refers to the lapsed person due to the preceding clause structure, but the Latin contrasts the lapsed person who obtains martyrdom with the heretic who, if killed outside the Church, cannot receive rewards. The English should make clear that 'ille' is the heretic/schismatic.
problems.fix: but if the heretic is killed outside the Church, he cannot arrive at the rewards of the Church.
problems.ruling: 'ille' refers to heretic/schismatic, but English 'if he is killed' ambiguously suggests the lapsed person, misleading the reader.

edits.old: but if he is killed outside the Church, he cannot arrive at the rewards of the Church.
edits.new: but if the heretic is killed outside the Church, he cannot arrive at the rewards of the Church.

fixed: The Latin 'ille' refers to the heretic/schismatic, not the lapsed person; the English 'he' was ambiguous after the preceding clause about the lapsed person. Changed to 'the heretic' to make the contrast clear.

last_rejected.quote: "You reject the commandment of God, so that you may establish your own tradition" (Mark 7:9)
last_rejected.source_quote: reicitis mandatum Dei, ut traditionem uestram statuatis
last_rejected.why: Quote matches Mark 7:9 in substance but Cyprian likely cites a composite; Mark 7:9 reads 'ye reject the commandment of God'.
last_rejected.fix: "You reject the commandment of God, so that you may establish your own tradition" (Mark 7:9)
last_rejected.ruling: Mark 7:9 matches source Latin closely; 'composite' claim speculative, no meaning changed or reader misled.

last_rejected.quote: entices sheep away from the shepherd
last_rejected.why: 'sollicitat' means 'incites, stirs up, agitates, solicits'—the heretic actively solicits/draws away sheep, not merely 'entices'
last_rejected.fix: draws sheep away from the shepherd
last_rejected.ruling: 'entices' is within 'sollicitat' normal range; both mean drawing away. Mere preference, not major error.
